What is Data Modelling?

Structuring data for efficient storage, retrieval and analysis.

  1. Data modelling is the process of creating visual representation of a system or database to illustrate the relationships between data elements.
  2. helps in understanding data requirements, improving communication, ensuring data integrity, optimized queries and scalability.

Types of Data Models

  • Conceptual Data Models: High-level overview of the system, focusing on business concepts.
    • Example: Entity-Relationship (ER) diagrams.
  • Logical Data Models: Detailed view of data structures and relationships, independent of physical implementation.
    • Example: Normalized tables and relationships.
  • Physical Data Models: Implementation details for databases, including tables, columns and indexes.
    • Example: SQL database schema.

Data Modelling for Data Engineers

Data modelling determines:

  • "How data is stored"
  • "How fast it can be queried"
  • "How scalable the system becomes"
  • "How easy analytics becomes"

Not only drawing ER diagrams, it affects:

  • Pipeline complexity
  • Query Performance
  • Cloud cost
  • Dashboard speed
  • Maintainability

Bad model = slow dashboards, expensive compute and fragile pipelines

Relational Database

Structured & Schema-Based(Tables, Rows, Columns).

Uses ACID Transactions(Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability).

Joins multiple tables for complex queries.

Examples:PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server.

NoSQL Database

Schema-less, designed for scalability and speed.

Flexible structures (key-value, document, columnar, graph).

Optimized for distributed architectures & Big Data.

Examples:MongoDB, Google BigQuery

Types of NoSQL Models

  • Key-value pairs (like a dictionary in Python).
    • Example:Cache for web sessions.
  • Document Store:
    • JSON-like documents (MongoDB).
    • Example:Storing user profiles in a social media app.
  • Columnar Store:
    • Stores data in columns instead of rows
    • Example:Data warehouses (Google BigQuery).
  • Graph Databases:
    • Optimized for relationships
    • Example:LinkedIn’s friend recommendation system.

Dimensional Modelling

  • Organizes data into Facts and Dimensions.
    • Facts = measurable events
    • Dimensions = descriptive context
  • Instead of modelling everything around normalization and minimal redundancy, we model around business questions
  • Optimized for Data Warehouses & Business Intelligence (BI).
  • Used for analytics (reporting, dashboards, KPIs).

Data Modelling Process

Benefits of Data Modelling

  • Improved Communication: Facilitates better understanding between stakeholders and developers.
  • Better System Design: Ensures data integrity, consistency, accuracy and efficiency.
  • Scalability and Maintenance: Easier updates and scalability of systems

Data Normalization

  • Reduces data redundancy and prevents anomalies.
  • Divides data into smaller tables & defines relationships -> Ensures data integrity and reduces storage costs.
  • Ensures consistency in transactional databases.

What is Data Organization?

Data organization refers to the method of arranging data in a structured format to facilitate efficient access, management and analysis

This is essential for effective data management, retrieval and analysis

Methods of Data Organization

  • Hierarchical Organization: Tree-like structure with parent-child relationships.
    • Example: XML data structure.
  • Relational Organization: Tables with rows and columns, using keys to establish relationships.
    • Example: Relational databases like MySQL.
  • Network Organization: Complex relationships between data nodes, allowing multiple parent-child connections.
    • Example: Network databases.
  • Object-Oriented Organization: Grouping data into objects, encapsulating both data and behaviour.
    • Example: Object-oriented databases.

Challenges in Data Modelling

Complexity: Managing complex data structures and relationships.

Changing Requirements: Adapting models to evolving business needs.

Data Quality: Ensuring data accuracy, consistency, and completeness.

Integration: Integrating data from multiple sources and systems.

Performance: Optimizing models for efficient data retrieval and processing.

Data Modelling Best Practices

Understand Business Requirements: Collaborate with stakeholders to gather detailed requirements.

Use Standardized Notations: Employ consistent and widely-recognized notations (e.g., ER diagrams, UML).

Iterative Approach: Continuously refine models based on feedback and changing requirements.

Documentation: Maintain comprehensive documentation for future reference and maintenance.

Validation and Testing: Regularly validate and test models to ensure accuracy and performance.
